Hi Oliver — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap & open items so we have alignment before I loop in ops/solutions for a draft quote.

Call summary (high level)
- Workload: customer-facing summarization + Q&A (hybrid retrieval + generation).
- Expected steady-state monthly volume: ~6,000,000,000 tokens / month (6B total; ~20% prompts, 80% generations).
- Burst/peak: short spikes up to ~1,200 tokens/sec for 10–15 minutes during peak traffic; sustained peak window expected ~400 tok/sec for 1–2 hours/day.
- Typical sequence lengths: prompts ~150 tokens, generations ~700 tokens (avg request ~850 tokens).
- Initial compliance/iso requirement: VPC-only Private/Dedicated deployment.

Budget & commercial guidance we discussed
- Target committed budget: $60k–$90k / month (looking for committed reserved pricing).
- Target unit goal: target $/1M tokens in the ballpark of $150–$350 depending on reserved footprint and quantization.

Open / ask from Acme I want to confirm before I send preliminary SKUs:
1) Final confirmation of monthly token volume tolerance (6B ± 20%) — can you confirm November baseline vs expected steady state?
2) Preferred GPU family: are you set on H100-class for latency, or would A100-80B be acceptable if it materially improves price?
3) Any hard p95 latency SLO? You mentioned sub-350ms for interactive calls — confirm if that is strict.
4) Any procurement timing or legal constraints (PO terms / required SLA embargo)?

Attachments: I asked you to share the token histogram (thanks if you can attach raw distribution). I’ve attached a short worksheet that our sales ops team will use to map to reserved SKUs.

Next steps
- Once you confirm items 1–3 I’ll pull Marissa and Avery in for a sizing + cost estimate and we’ll produce a 1-page committed-reservation proposal (SKU, expected throughput, estimated $/1M tokens).

Thanks — Hannah

Hannah / Avery — ran a quick sizing pass and attached a summarized worksheet (redwood-dedicated-estimate-20261120.xlsx). High-level notes below; these are conservative and assume standard continuous-batching + prefix KV caching for prompt reuse.

Option A — 4 x H100 (80GB) reserved (baseline)
- Expected sustained throughput: ~900 tokens/sec total (multi-tenant routing internal to Acme flow assumed)
- Burst headroom via autoscale to ~1,400 tok/sec (with short-duration GPU burst pool)
- Latency: p95 ~280–340ms (depends on batch depth, prompt lengths)
- Estimated effective cost: ~$220 / 1M tokens (committed monthly estimate)
- Monthly committed price: ~$78,000 / month (fits their $75–95k range)

Option B — 8 x H100 reserved (aggressive)
- Sustained throughput: ~1,800 tok/sec
- Burst headroom: 2,800+ tok/sec
- Latency: p95 ~200–260ms
- Estimated cost: ~$130 / 1M tokens
- Monthly committed price: ~$160,000 / month (above stated target; propose staged ramp)

Option C — Mixed fleet: 3 x H100 + 6 x A100-80GB (cost-optimized)
- Sustained throughput: ~1,100 tok/sec (hot routing to H100 for low-latency flows)
- Burst headroom: ~1,900 tok/sec
- Latency: p95 ~240–360ms (hot routes meet SLA)
- Estimated cost: ~$155 / 1M tokens
- Monthly committed price: ~$95,000 / month (near their stretch budget; better unit economics than pure H100 baseline)

Assumptions / notes:
- Token economics estimate includes GPU infra amortization, SW overhead, cluster redundancy (N+1), and expected cache hit rates of ~18% on KV/prefix reuse.
- We assumed mixed quantization (int8 where possible) for A100 paths; H100 runs Q4-optimized kernels for best-latency.
- We included a 10% operational buffer to account for peak smoothing and autoscale inefficiency.

Recommendation to present to Acme: start with Option A (4 x H100) as a baseline committed SKU that fits their immediate budget & latency needs, with an explicit 60–90 day ramp clause and option to add A100 background capacity. That keeps initial monthly under $80k but preserves upgrade path. If they want best unit economics up front, show Option C as the price-performance compromise.

What I’ll attach to the external: a 1-page SKU + commitment table and a short explainer of expected $/1M token math (we can show both raw and amortized unit costs). Shall I turn this into a short PDF for procurement?

—Marissa
